Color identity: WU | Bracket: 4+ (Ruthless) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {1}{U}{U}
Produces: Infinite turns; Lock
Start: Exchange of Words (hand); Wormfang Manta (battlefield); Meneldor, Swift Savior (battlefield); Opalescence (battlefield)
Prerequisites: Meneldor does not have summoning sickness and cannot be blocked by an opponent.
Steps: Cast Exchange of Words by paying {1}{U}{U}.
  When Exchange of Words enters the battlefield, it triggers, exchanging the text boxes of it and Wormfang Manta.
  Deal combat damage to an opponent using Meneldor, triggering it, blinking Exchange of Words.
  Exchange of Words leaves and enters the battlefield, triggering the second ability it gained from Wormfang Manta's textbox as well as its own ability.
  Resolve the first Exchange of Words trigger, causing you to take an extra turn after this one.
  Resolve the second Exchange of Words trigger, exchanging the text boxes of it and Wormfang Manta.
  Repeat from step 3 during each turn.

  Exchange of Words leaves and enters the battlefield, triggering the second ability it gained from Wormfang Manta's textbox as well as its own ability.
  Resolve the first Exchange of Words trigger, causing you to take an extra turn after this one.
  Resolve the second Exchange of Words trigger, exchanging the text boxes of it and Wormfang Manta.
  Repeat from step 3 during each turn.

## Combo 3742-3839-4344
Cards: Phantom Steed + Changeling Hero + Lumbering Battlement
Color identity: WU | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 39 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {0} plus the mana cost of the creature in your hand

  When Lumbering Battlement leaves the battlefield, Phantom Steed is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: Due to differences in card templating between the various banisher effects (linked triggered abilities vs "until" clause), steps 3, 5, and 7 may return the creature to the battlefield during the resolution of the preceding step rather than creating a separate event. This should not affect the overall execution of the combo, only how many objects pass through the stack (and thus rounds of priority available per loop).
